title: What happens when you hit send
note: One continuous shot, so one scene. TheLifecycle is the whole film: the set is built once in lifecycle_set.py and the camera flies through it. There is deliberately nothing to concatenate — cutting between scenes is what this format is built to avoid. The budget moved from 45s to 50s when the end-of-film beat was rebuilt: one lap of the plant, then ten decode cycles inside the box, one word each. The loop is the point of the film, so it is not compressed to defend the old number. It then moved 50s → 60s for the narration pass, under a HARD 60.0s cap set by the user: 9.27s went where the script's lines land - 7.95s as stillness after content settles, and 1.32s as honestly slower motion in the two places the plan authorised it (REQUEST_LAP_RUN_TIME 1.6->2.2, CYCLES_EXPLICIT's lap 0.38->0.56), both inside the pull-back, which is the one stretch with no still frame to hold on. The script itself was cut from 315 words to 131 to fit that cap — the film was not stretched to the script. 60 is a ceiling, not a target with tolerance; if a future change pushes the measured figure over it, take the time out of the after and client beats first.
